title: How fast to attack: forcing now or calm first
outcomes: Chooses between forcing play now and a calm strengthening move, and gives the reason (king in the centre, or sound cover)
Explains why a calm move that adds an attacker is not passive
Tests whether a defender's piece already in place changes the right pace
Recognises a position with no attack to pace because material is simply free

steps.text:
How fast should an attack go? Two speeds.
**Quick:** forcing moves now (checks, captures, sacrifices), because the king is still in the centre or the defenders are not yet near.
**Moderate:** a calm move that brings one more piece to bear, because forcing moves would only trade your attackers away.
A calm move that adds an attacker is not passive.

steps.caption: Black to move. White's king is still on e1 and has not castled.

line.say: Check at once, while the king is still in the centre.
White takes the bishop with the queen.

claims.statement: Bxf2+ is the engine's best move.
Along the engine line Bxf2+ nets Black at least 4 points.
The white king is in the centre.
The calm Qd5 is far worse.

steps.text: **Moderate pace.** When the king is sheltered behind pawns, forcing moves often run out of pieces. A calm move that adds one more attacker can beat a check. Ask: which of my pieces is not yet attacking? This is a *rule of thumb*. Whether to attack at all is the lesson 'Count before you attack: attack now, not yet, or no'.

**Conditions.** Quick when the king is still in the centre or open files point at it. Moderate when the king is sheltered and you can add an attacker.
**Fails.** A slow move while the king can still castle gives him time. A calm plan fails when the defender's piece is already in place: test that before trusting the plan.

steps.title: The calm plan, and what can break it
steps.prompt: In the first position a calm move wins. Predict what happens when one black pawn is added, and when material is simply free so there is no attack to pace.
Take the last position you attacked in. Was the king still in the centre? Did you pick quick or moderate, and what did the defender do in reply?
